title: Mac and Cheese
description: Mac and Cheese is a comforting baked pasta dish featuring tender macaroni coated in a rich, velvety cheese sauce made with Parmigiano-Reggiano, Fontina, and mozzarella. Finished with a golden, crispy panko topping, this restaurant-quality version delivers the perfect balance of creamy, cheesy, and crunchy textures.

ingredients.title: Pasta
items: 400 g (14 oz) elbow macaroni or cavatappi

ingredients.title: Cheese Sauce
items: Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Optional: 1/2 cup Pecorino Romano for extra sharpness

instruction.title: Step 1 – Cook the Pasta
steps: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente.
Drain, toss with a tiny drizzle of olive oil to prevent sticking, and set aside.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Make the Cheese Sauce
steps: In a medium saucepan, melt butter over medium heat.
Whisk in flour and cook for 1–2 minutes to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in warm milk and cream until smooth and thickened (about 5–6 minutes).
Stir in Dijon mustard, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Lower heat and fold in Parmigiano-Reggiano, Fontina, mozzarella, and Pecorino Romano until creamy and silky. Taste and adjust seasoning.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Assemble
steps: Combine pasta with cheese sauce, ensuring every piece is coated.
Pour into a buttered baking dish.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Prepare the Topping
steps: Mix panko breadcrumbs with melted butter, Parmigiano-Reggiano, and parsley.
Sprinkle evenly over the mac and cheese.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Bake
steps: Bake uncovered for 20–25 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Optional: broil 1–2 minutes for an extra-crispy top.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Serve
steps: Let sit 5 minutes before serving to set slightly.
Garnish with extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano or parsley for presentation.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot as a main course or side dish.
Pair with roasted vegetables or a crisp green salad.
Enjoy with garlic bread for a complete meal.

chefTips: Cheese selection: Fontina gives creaminess, Parmigiano adds sharpness, mozzarella ensures stretchiness, Pecorino Romano adds bold flavor.
Roux care: Don't let it brown; keep it pale for a silky sauce.
Texture: Use panko for crunch—freshly made breadcrumbs give the best results.
Finishing touch: A light drizzle of truffle oil before serving elevates it to gourmet level.
